narrative.title: Reverse-Engineering the Signal Alphabet
narrative.scenario: Signals interception recovered a sorted word list from an alien civilisation using the first k earth-equivalent letters. Comparing each neighbouring word pair at its first differing position reveals one before-the-other fact; chaining all those facts should yield one total letter precedence — provided the intercepted list isn't self-contradictory.
narrative.inputFormat: A list dict of N words sorted by the alien alphabet, and an integer k — the number of letters (a..) in use.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the alien character order as a string of k lowercase letters.
constraints: All words consist only of the first k lowercase letters

testCases.explanation: baa<abcd pins b<a; abcd<abca pins d<c; abca<cab pins a<c — topologically b,d,a,c.
The five comparisons chain into the order w, e, r, t, f.

hintLevels: Level 1: Only the FIRST differing character between adjacent words carries ordering information.
Level 2: Each comparison contributes one directed edge; a Kahn's pass over the letter graph is the answer.
Level 3: Letters untouched by any comparison simply append where their indegree clears; a drain shorter than k exposes the contradiction.
